A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaskedLRM research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched reliably despite figure rearrangements and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ABO/GSO reconstruction measurements, runtime comparisons, qualitative mesh-editing results, and geometric-supervision and masking ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds reconstruction comparisons, editing comparisons with concurrent methods, and quantitative CLIP editing results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same conditional transformer, 3D-consistent masking, triplane/SDF decoding, reconstruction and perceptual losses, two-stage training, and editing procedure. The revised explanations do not establish an algorithmic or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Objaverse training data, ABO/GSO reconstruction evaluation, and localized editing of the same represented object types. The additional comparisons and CLIP scores do not establish a new dataset or distinct task. Removing training-subset details does not establish changed data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SyncDreamer and Wonder3D to Figure 3, PrEditor3D and Instant3Dit to editing and runtime comparisons, and InstantMesh NeRF/Mesh rows to Table 1. New Table 3 compares against Instant3Dit and MagicClay. Conversely, the masked Zero-123++/InstantMesh comparator shown in v1 Figures 3–4 is removed.

E3.justification: New Table 3 introduces prompt-matched editing evaluation using CLIP cosine similarity averaged across views, with ViT-L-14 and ViT-BigG-14 encoders. The existing reconstruction metrics, 6/8 input-view evaluations, ten evaluation poses, and documented training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The geometric-supervision and 25% random-patch masking ablations are retained; v2's new main-text masking paragraph summarizes existing appendix evidence. However, Figure 3 replaces v1's original-versus-masked Zero-123++ diagnostic with artifact comparisons involving Zero-123++, SyncDreamer, and Wonder3D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed results, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new CLIP averages across views are evaluation aggregates, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparison evidence while retaining the original MaskedLRM/MeshLRM reconstruction scores. Table 3 reports CLIP scores of 0.323/0.337 for MaskedLRM, 0.303/0.309 for Instant3Dit, and 0.285/0.286 for MagicClay across two encoders. Table 1 adds InstantMesh GSO results, and Table 2 adds approximately 6-second Instant3Dit and 80-second PrEditor3D runtimes. New qualitative findings replace some masked-baseline results; these are additions and removals, not improved scores for the unchanged proposed model.

T1.justification: The tokenization, masking, transformer, rendering, and loss formulations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; the new CLIP evaluation does not introduce theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the speed claim from 10× to 2–10×. The introduction explicitly claims generalization to arbitrary inference masks and narrows the contrast with other LRMs to approaches trained without masking. The central conditional-reconstruction and mesh-editing contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 explains that its reconstruction advantage over InstantMesh is expected because it receives multiple views, adds face-detail blurring versus chair examples to the limitations, and attributes PrEditor3D's runtime to multiple pretrained models. The appendix also acknowledges the absence of a standard editing benchmark.

D1.justification: v2 removes the 480k training-subset size, quality-filtering description, Sketchfab-exclusion footnote, and statement that Table 2 runtimes were all measured on one A100 GPU. These are losses of documentation, not demonstrated changes in execution. Detailed architecture, optimizer, training hardware, epochs, learning rates, and the project link remain.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including Instant3Dit, PrEditor3D, SyncDreamer, and Wonder3D. The introduction and related work more explicitly distinguish MaskedLRM from concurrent diffusion-based editing and NeRFiller's fixed per-scene masks. This updates the existing research positioning without replacing its central novelty argument.

P1.justification: v2 revises selected introduction, comparison, and limitations paragraphs, splits the contributions into three bullets, broadens the InstantMesh subsection to LRM-based methods, and removes appendix section numbering. The overall section sequence and most methodological exposition remain stable.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: v1 Figure 5 becomes the opening figure, the original teaser disappears, Figure 3 is replaced, the bird-comparison figure loses a row, and a concurrent-method comparison is added. Tables 1–2 expand and Table 3 is new. Appendix Figures 8–9 exchange order, and the NeRFiller display changes from vertical to horizontal.

improvement.justification: Comparisons with PrEditor3D and Instant3Dit and the first quantitative editing scores strengthen evidence for the central editing contribution. Explicit discussion of unequal input information and fine-detail failures also improves interpretation. The gains are limited by missing sample/view counts for the CLIP evaluation, removal of the masked baseline, and reduced training-data and runtime-hardware documentation. Overall, v2 provides a modestly stronger evaluation, without resolving these reproducibility limitations.
